patterns.title: AAL2 device-session bootstrap must not require an RLS-protected SELECT
patterns.rootCause: A representation-returning INSERT for a newly bootstrapped device session conflicted with the table's hardened active-session SELECT RLS predicate after successful TOTP authentication.
patterns.prevention: Preserve owner+AAL2 checks and an INSERT with explicit revoked_at:null and Prefer:return=minimal; cover the post-MFA bootstrap and RLS failure boundary.

patterns.title: Imported Lending data must be normalized at runtime
patterns.rootCause: Lending selectors treated unvalidated historical JSON as if TypeScript types had already validated person, entries, dates and numeric fields.
patterns.prevention: Normalize or skip malformed legacy rows at the selector boundary; preserve valid/minimal receivable summary semantics without logging financial payloads.

patterns.title: Shared form controls must not drift into page-specific skins
patterns.rootCause: Default input/control styling diverged across Quick Entry, authentication and editors instead of sharing design-system primitives and semantic tokens.
patterns.prevention: Modify the shared primitive/token owner, inspect sibling consumers and verify Light/Dark, focus, invalid, disabled and relevant responsive states.

patterns.title: CI fan-out should not repeat expensive checks on every UI correction
patterns.rootCause: High-churn pushes and overlapping workflow ownership generated redundant full validation, even where review-ready gates or a single owner were sufficient.
patterns.prevention: Keep core CI and security gates; defer heavy rendered/performance/Windows checks to final review head, cancel superseded runs, and run targeted local preflight first.

patterns.title: Windows packaged backend must boot through its CommonJS bridge
patterns.rootCause: The Electron host appeared alive while its bundled ESM backend failed on a CommonJS require('tty'); setup-path CI bypassed live packaged backend verification.
patterns.prevention: Keep a Node createRequire bridge in the packaged ESM backend, capture sanitized startup errors and validate live backend readiness through real first-run configuration.

patterns.title: Product migration must preserve owner category trees
patterns.rootCause: Schema-v3 product migration rebuilt settings but discarded the persisted expense and income category-tree extensions.
patterns.prevention: Preserve both trees across load/import migration and keep older flat-category documents compatible without rewriting history.

patterns.title: Initial account metadata write must target an unambiguous constraint
patterns.rootCause: PL/pgSQL account_id output variable made ON CONFLICT(owner_user_id, account_id) ambiguous in the revision-zero insert path.
patterns.prevention: Use the named primary-key constraint on conflict and preserve SECURITY INVOKER, owner+AAL2 and 0->1 / 1->2 revision checks.

patterns.title: Durable history audit constraint must admit undo and redo
patterns.rootCause: The audit-log action constraint admitted save/import/backup but not undo/redo already used by canonical history RPCs.
patterns.prevention: Keep audit-action and RPC semantics aligned in forward-only migrations, and test both undo and redo without rewriting financial history.

patterns.title: Vercel plain API functions need an independent supported TS project
patterns.rootCause: Vercel's plain Node function packager could not resolve the root TypeScript 7 project-reference toolchain.
patterns.prevention: Keep the API-local supported compiler, tsconfig without references and separate API dependency/typecheck gate.

patterns.title: Operational upstream outages must not revoke valid auth sessions
patterns.rootCause: Supabase request, timeout and 5xx failures were classified as bad credentials or expired sessions, clearing otherwise valid cookies.
patterns.prevention: Differentiate bounded upstream/unavailable/429 failures from real 401/invalid credentials and preserve browser sessions on operational failures.

patterns.title: Finance document limits must fit deployment request and response budgets
patterns.rootCause: Accepted finance documents could exceed Vercel's 4.5 MB Functions body ceiling and malformed imported nested data reached consumers.
patterns.prevention: Keep shared 4 MiB budget on read/save/import paths and validate nested financial structures before persistence.

patterns.title: Editing loan payments must preserve the linked loan identity
patterns.rootCause: Quick Add recreated edited payment events without loanId so existing installments stopped counting toward loan progress.
patterns.prevention: Carry linked loan identity through edit/delete and derive loan progress from one canonical linked-event helper.

patterns.title: Derived snapshots and receivables must ignore incidental input ordering
patterns.rootCause: Balance baseline relied on array order and Lending Map.set silently overwrote repeated historical persons.
patterns.prevention: Pick latest eligible date explicitly and aggregate duplicated legacy lending identities instead of replacing them.

patterns.title: Recurring and zero-valued settings must use effective state
patterns.rootCause: Dashboard read raw recurring seeds without overrides and used truthy defaults that silently replaced valid 0 budgets or 0% goals.
patterns.prevention: Consume effective recurring items with overrides/custom entries and use nullish defaults; guard zero denominator display.

patterns.title: Finance reporting date must refresh after local midnight
patterns.rootCause: A module-level TODAY constant stayed stale while the application remained open across a local date boundary.
patterns.prevention: Use reactive local-date refresh including tab resume and daylight-saving changes without overwriting an explicitly chosen reporting month.

patterns.title: Production smoke health assertions must follow released identity
patterns.rootCause: A product rename changed the health payload but production smoke still expected the old app name, failing healthy deployments.
patterns.prevention: Keep release smoke's expected app identity synchronized with the published health contract while retaining header and deployment assertions.

patterns.title: Local proxy must preserve browser-facing Origin and Host consistency
patterns.rootCause: Bare Vite API proxy forwarded an upstream Host while browser Origin used the frontend port, causing 403 ORIGIN_MISMATCH on login.
patterns.prevention: Forward the browser-facing host/protocol through the reviewed proxy headers and keep origin enforcement enabled for cookie mutations.

patterns.title: Production API routes must fit the serverless function-count limit
patterns.rootCause: Deploying another standalone API function exceeded Vercel Hobby's serverless function budget and blocked the exact release.
patterns.prevention: Route compatible handlers through reviewed existing functions/rewrite contracts and assert the current deployment function budget.

patterns.title: Lazy page and chunk failures need a recoverable workspace boundary
patterns.rootCause: Suspense handled pending lazy imports but not rejected chunks or page render exceptions, leaving the workspace blank or unrecoverable.
patterns.prevention: Keep page-local ErrorBoundary around route Suspense with retry, navigation recovery and privacy-safe error text.

patterns.title: Domain input semantics must be consistent before persistence
patterns.rootCause: Quick Add, reconciliation, lending attribution, split positivity and loan ranges had UI/server semantic mismatches despite structurally valid input.
patterns.prevention: Validate empty reconciliation versus zero, required lending attribution, positive split parts and bounded loan/settings semantics on both client and server.

patterns.title: Rules action taxonomy must match eligible transaction kinds and preview precedence
patterns.rootCause: The only active automation editor offered expense categories but its shared matching engine also applied expense category/subcategory actions to default-category income events; preview and first-match ordering could falsely match income.
patterns.prevention: Reject income matches for expense category/subcategory rules, preserve note-only income rules and current history, and ensure preview, first-match and apply share the eligibility rule.

patterns.title: Command focus must target the visible responsive owner without refocusing on unrelated renders
patterns.rootCause: A desktop Command Palette action targeted the CSS-hidden legacy Planning scheduled list rather than the visible approved table. The first correction then used freshly allocated filtered arrays in effect dependencies and repeatedly stole keyboard focus when the palette was opened again.
patterns.prevention: Route named targets to the actually visible responsive surface, extend its pagination and make the target programmatically focusable. Derive primitive hook dependencies and consume each command-key focus once so subsequent user interactions retain focus.

patterns.title: Rendered CRUD receipts must follow durable owner status, not obsolete success copy
patterns.rootCause: Two successive coherent review runs were blocked after otherwise successful finance/security/Windows checks because old rendered CRUD deletion waits asserted obsolete literal success messages (first Cards secure-vault cleanup, then Settings account deletion), rather than the current domain owner's durable receipt.
patterns.prevention: Before a full rendered review matrix, keep the source regression guard matching the owning UI receipt and assert both absence of the deleted entity and explicit durable success with the confirmation dialog dismissed; never replace the wait with row absence alone or weaken the underlying finance/vault checks.

patterns.title: Unsaved form and receipt review edits must not disappear on modal close or draft switch
patterns.rootCause: Contextual Quick Entry and the local OCR review had direct close, backdrop and draft-switch routes that discarded edited fields without the explicit confirmation already present in generic QuickAdd.
patterns.prevention: Route all close/cancel/Escape/backdrop and receipt-selection/manual handoff paths through shared destructive-discard confirmation; keep focus with the active dialog, preserve local unsaved fields when cancelled and do not restart finance writes or overwrite a dirty receipt with capture.

patterns.title: Clipboard fallback must confirm success and erase temporary copy fields
patterns.rootCause: Sensitive-card copy treated the legacy execCommand false return as success and did not guarantee cleanup of a transient clipboard textarea on exceptions. Related IBAN copy had the same exception cleanup risk.
patterns.prevention: Use one explicitly user-triggered clipboard helper, check native or legacy copy acknowledgement, clear/remove temporary fields in finally, never claim success for rejected writes, and announce failure through accessible error semantics without exposing copied contents.

patterns.title: Direct recurring Storage registration must bind immutable key and MIME in PostgreSQL
patterns.rootCause: The invoker registration RPC checked public Storage path format and object existence without proving the path belonged to the supplied asset key and MIME; direct owner+AAL2 SQL writes could bypass API validation and misregister another logo.
patterns.prevention: Use a row-level CHECK binding services/<asset-key>.<MIME-extension> across direct RPC and metadata writes, retain owner+AAL2 RLS, and prove direct PostgREST AAL1/nonowner denials and AAL2 key/MIME mutation rejection in isolated local Supabase.

patterns.title: Direct provider Storage registration must bind owner directory, generated key and MIME
patterns.rootCause: The authenticated invoker RPC checked only whether a Storage object existed; direct callers could register another provider image under a new key or mismatched MIME, while API readback enforced stricter provenance.
patterns.prevention: Validate canonical server-issued keys and exact provider/key/MIME Storage paths in the existing SECURITY INVOKER RPC and a forward-only CHECK for generated rows, keep curated legacy assets untouched, and prove direct owner/nonowner/AAL1 negatives on the isolated local stack.

patterns.title: Do not purge recurring logo Storage after an unverified finance commit
patterns.rootCause: A finance write may commit before its transport/history receipt disappears. The recurring editor deleted a freshly uploaded logo whenever a finance Promise rejected, even if the committed finance reference used it.
patterns.prevention: Purge only after explicit precommit REVISION_CONFLICT, preserve uncertain Storage references, block repeat upload until finance reload, and preflight pending/conflicted finance state before any Storage write.

patterns.title: Block repeat Quick Entry submissions after uncertain finance acknowledgment
patterns.rootCause: Generic and contextual Quick Entry disabled duplicate submissions only while the first promise was pending. A lost finance response after commit left the button enabled to submit a new event ID.
patterns.prevention: Classify only explicit precommit REVISION_CONFLICT as proven rejection. After an ambiguous post-dispatch response, retain the editor warning and disable Save until the owner closes and reviews persisted state; preserve retries after local validation errors.

patterns.title: Reject false-positive vault write receipts and protect uncertain encrypted updates
patterns.rootCause: The card vault accepted any 2xx body as durable save/deletion evidence and told the owner that transport loss could not have changed encrypted card data. The editor allowed a second write after an unknown outcome.
patterns.prevention: Require an exact saved/deleted response with expected last-four provenance, classify lost 0/408/429/5xx and malformed success receipts as unverified, lock repeated card-secret updates until secure reload and never claim rollback on a lost reply.

patterns.title: Same-turn recurring/provider binary uploads must not allocate duplicate Storage keys
patterns.rootCause: Recurring Save used only asynchronous React editBusy state, and exported recurring/provider binary-upload clients had no synchronous per-target in-flight lock. Two same-task saves or direct client calls could dispatch duplicate PUT requests while the first independently generated Storage key was still unverified.
patterns.prevention: Acquire a synchronous recurring-item or provider/role/variant slot before dispatching the first binary PUT, reject concurrent same-target calls without issuing a second write, retain independent target concurrency, and clear the lock only for the original auth epoch. Add a RecurringPage save ref guard before any upload or finance writer and keep uncertain-receipt safeguards unchanged.

patterns.title: New provider asset receipts must prove the exact generated-key Storage URL
patterns.rootCause: The browser provider upload accepted an HTTP-200 asset with matching provider-generated key, role, variant, MIME, filename and byte count but any otherwise allowed HTTPS URL. Its full catalog readback validated those metadata fields yet never checked that the returned URL belonged to the generated key's immutable Storage object, allowing a false-green save or broken/foreign image.
patterns.prevention: Require the server-defined public financial-provider-assets/providers/{provider}/{assetKey}.{MIME-extension} path for newly generated upload receipts and for those exact uploaded keys in the complete catalog. Keep curated legacy provider artwork on its prior compatible URL contract. Use a forged correct-key/wrong-path negative at the actual provider editor, independent unit negatives, and synthetic same-origin Storage-image CDP fixtures rather than weakening a validator to accommodate stale QA URLs.

patterns.title: Lost recurring asset release acknowledgement must not trigger a second DELETE
patterns.rootCause: The recurring browser client treated transport failure or HTTP 408/429/5xx after DELETE as an ordinary retryable error. The server release can deactivate the row before Storage deletion and purge; its public asset catalog reads only active rows, so an empty catalog following an ambiguous response cannot prove the Storage object or inactive registry row was purged.
patterns.prevention: Synchronous per-key release lock; treat lost/408/429/5xx/invalid-200 receipts as unverified and block same-key replay in the current auth scope without claiming success from an active-only catalog. Accept success only after server {ok:true} (which follows confirmed Storage deletion and row purge) plus a fresh owner-scoped active-catalog absence check. Preserve definite 4xx retry and old-auth-epoch isolation; guard failed Storage cleanup and double DELETE negatives.

patterns.title: RLS-hidden recurring asset purge row cannot count as confirmed deletion
patterns.rootCause: The server checked current owner+AAL2 only after ambiguous purge RPC responses and only before the exact-row GET. A normal HTTP-200/void purge result followed by an RLS-hidden empty GET after owner/device revocation could be falsely acknowledged as definitive Storage+registry cleanup. The sibling provider and recurring upload compensation paths also treated an empty exact-key read as absence without checking that the same session retained owner+AAL2 visibility; a masked Storage 404 could be mistaken for confirmed cleanup. The shared metadata error parser also trusted embedded SQLSTATE/message markers before testing the HTTP transport status, allowing a 5xx/408/429 to appear as definite rollback.
patterns.prevention: Keep exact-key inactive-inclusive readback, then independently require a true current owner+AAL2 predicate after that read before reporting success for either ordinary or ambiguous purge receipts. Missing/revoked/nonboolean owner proof fails closed; never reissue Storage DELETE to reconcile a lost receipt. Regression matrix covers normal-200 and postcommit-5xx with RLS-empty, retained/inaccessible rows and bounded release authorization. For definite registration rejection compensation, require fresh original-token owner+AAL2 before each bounded DELETE and after an acknowledged 200/404; never delete on failed/malformed owner proof or return the definite rejection as clean when authorization disappears. Both asset types preserve ambiguous-registration no-delete behavior. Treat upstream HTTP 408/429/5xx as ambiguous before interpreting any PostgreSQL marker. Test both artwork registration paths with contradictory validation, conflict and authorization payloads; do not delete or retry on an empty initial readback.

patterns.title: Rendered recurring evidence must wait for shared collection entrance completion
patterns.rootCause: The actual-browser real-stack screenshot was taken as soon as finance DOM data appeared. The Recurring summary grid, active table and paused list use 170–190ms shared staggered CSS entrance with child delays, so CDP could capture low-opacity content before animation completion.
patterns.prevention: Before the Recurring persisted-state screenshot, wait for the genuinely visible grid/list/table rows to have no running rh-bank-in/rh-backdrop-in animation and computed opacity >=0.995. Keep production animation and finance state unchanged; reject screenshot evidence with transient invisible rows. Assert helper placement and gate in real-stack browser source tests.

patterns.title: Report-to-credit navigation evidence must wait for route opacity and collection entrance
patterns.rootCause: The actual Chromium Real Stack Reports credit drillthrough screenshot was captured as soon as the destination heading and purchase row appeared. AppShell AnimatePresence motion.div remained at fractional opacity during the 180ms route transition, washing out the entire credit card, numbers and heading despite correct settled content.
patterns.prevention: After verifying the actual card purchase row on the Credit route, wait for the live AppShell route wrapper, destination page and visible purchase row to reach full computed opacity and for bounded collection entrance animation to finish before capturing evidence. Never replace a valid product transition with global disabled motion or a guessed fixed sleep.

patterns.title: Read-only receipt status preflight permits concurrent cross-tab finance posting
patterns.rootCause: Two tabs could both see pending/ready in readonly IndexedDB preflight, then each dispatch a separate finance write before the local receipt was marked posted.
patterns.prevention: Acquire an atomic IndexedDB readwrite posting claim after input and linked-fee validation but before finance dispatch; retain unknown/crashed posting across reload; restore only on proven precommit finance conflict, preserve posted-before-local-delete and surface posting as non-repostable.

patterns.title: Provider image binding clear may treat RLS-hidden [] as confirmed deletion after revoked owner session
patterns.rootCause: The server accepted empty exact-slot readback as proof of cleared provider image binding on HTTP 200/void without an owner+AAL2 recheck; ambiguous 5xx checked ownership only before GET, leaving revocation between probe and readback unverified.
patterns.prevention: For both acknowledged and ambiguous provider-binding RPCs, validate the exact slot readback, then require fresh rheomiq_is_owner_aal2 === true before returning ok. Reject unavailable/false/malformed owner proof as unverified; no duplicate RPC or relaxed RLS.

patterns.title: Provider binary upload uncertainty resets on editor close and permits a second same-slot Storage key
patterns.rootCause: The client guarded concurrent provider binary PUTs only while a single request was in flight. After network loss, HTTP 408/429/5xx or a malformed HTTP 200 registration receipt, finally cleared the slot guard; reopening the provider editor allowed another non-idempotent upload of an independent freshly generated key even when the first Storage/DB write may have committed.
patterns.prevention: Quarantine the exact provider/role/variant slot for the originating authentication scope after any ambiguous binary upload. Reject new same-slot PUTs even with changed File objects; do not affect independent slots, proved precommit 400/403 rejections or a genuinely new auth scope. Ignore old-scope late outcomes. Explain the hold and safe manual catalog review in the existing provider warning, and cover the desktop/mobile screenshot states. Use same-origin nonblocking Web Locks for provider/recurring binary upload and recurring release when supported; retain the lock on ambiguous outcomes until the initiating live auth scope retires. Unsupported browsers keep existing local guards. Never persist private slot data or claim durable recovery after full browser teardown. Require actual same-origin two-tab native LockManager evidence after ambiguous provider upload and editor close, with zero competing same-slot writes and one independent-slot definite rejection.

patterns.title: Stale Card Vault read and write responses can cross a newer owner authentication scope
patterns.rootCause: Card Vault browser reads and encrypted save/delete mutations did not compare their originating auth epoch against the active scope after transport/body completion. An older successful reveal could populate PAN/CVV in a newer session; an old successful mutation could raise an incorrect new-scope saved receipt, and an old delayed 401 could dispatch auth-expired and invalidate a newer browser session.
patterns.prevention: Bind each Card Vault request to the global authenticated scope epoch. Check AFTER the response body settles but BEFORE notifyAuthExpired, discard any older response or transport result, and keep late legacy IndexedDB CVV fallback from returning a retired owner's secret. Classify stale write/delete receipts as unverified, never successful; preserve the normal current-scope definite 401/logout behavior. Never log/store PAN/CVV or weaken server owner+AAL2/device/RLS boundaries.

patterns.title: Retired write intent can dispatch under a newer authentication scope during preflight or shared progress notification
patterns.rootCause: saveAccountMetadata captured its auth epoch only after awaiting refreshAccountMetadata. A previous owner/session save waiting on a slow cold GET could be resumed after logout/reauth by a newer scope's freshly loaded catalog; the old call would then use the new owner revision and issue a PUT under the newer cookie.
patterns.prevention: Capture auth epoch before trackDatabaseWrite and any asynchronous catalog refresh. After a cold GET and immediately before the PUT, require that the initiating session epoch is still current; reject a retired action as a definitive pre-dispatch abort without classifying a write as committed or using a new owner revision. The shared save tracker must also capture the epoch before publishing progress and reject before invoking the write callback when a synchronous subscriber retires the session; cover provider metadata/binary/binding, recurring upload/release and Card Vault save/delete, as well as fresh explicit retry. Keep real acknowledged writes, revision conflicts, ambiguous post-dispatch receipts, MFA and RLS protections unchanged. Extend provenance to finance FIFO/reload/cursor/import/backup and provider/recurring multi-stage editors; ignore retired shared activity completions, and fence delayed JSON receipts before stale auth/PIN events. No stale operation may dispatch a next stage using a new cookie. Recheck scope after synchronous loading-state subscribers in all three metadata catalogs; recurring upload/release must use an epoch-bound forced readback so waiting for a pre-write GET cannot dispatch a read with newer credentials.
